text:
Avery (People Ops): Hey all :wave: Quick update: we've added an "Emergency Immediate-Family Support" policy for urgent caregiving situations (e.g., sudden hospitalization of spouse/child/parent). Key points below — please read and share with teams.

Avery (People Ops): TL;DR: Up to 10 days/year of short-notice emergency leave. First 5 days paid (company-paid), remaining up to 5 days can be taken as PTO or unpaid leave depending on your balance. We also added a small international emergency travel stipend for approved immediate-family travel. :heart:

Jordan (HR Lead): Eligibility: full-time employees after 30 days with Redwood. Contractors, please contact your engagement manager — we have a separate short-term support path.

Maya (Eng Manager): Thanks — is manager approval required before taking emergency leave? We sometimes need approvals when folks are in on-call rotations.

Avery (People Ops): Good Q. If it's a true emergency where the person can't secure pre-approval, take the leave and file a request as soon as you're able. For non-immediate emergencies, please request via the HR portal beforehand. We added an "urgent" flag to speed approvals.

Eli (Benefits): On pay: payroll will process the first 5 days as paid emergency leave. If you also use PTO, that will be applied after those 5 days if you choose. For the international travel stipend: submit a short request (one-paragraph) and receipts. Stipend cap is $800 per incident; we may make exceptions in extreme cases.

Maya (Eng Manager): Is there a shorter receipts rule for quick reimbursements? sometimes folks need cash for last-minute flights.

Avery (People Ops): For small immediate purchases related to arranging emergency travel (<= $250), we can fast-track without full receipts — a photo of the boarding pass + short note in the request is usually enough. For larger amounts or stipends, receipts are required within 30 days.

Sam (People Ops bot): Reminder scheduled: "Emergency Leave & Travel Policy webinar" on Mon 10AM PT. :bell: Add to calendar: <https://redwood-internal/events/emer-leave>

Jordan (HR Lead): Process steps (short):
1) Take necessary time.
2) Submit request in HR portal (choose "Emergency Immediate-Family Support").
3) Add urgent flag or email people-ops@redwood.com if you need same-day review.
4) Attach receipts/photo evidence within 30 days if requesting stipend.

Avery (People Ops): Documentation and examples have been added to the People Ops hub: <https://redwood-internal/hr/leave/emergency-support> — includes sample subject line for email and a template: 

```
Subject: Urgent: Family Emergency Leave — [Your Name]
Dates: [start] to [end (expected)]
Brief reason: [e.g., parent hospitalized, child surgery]
Contact during leave: [optional phone/email]
```

Avery (People Ops): Also a quick reminder about safety and travel: if you're travelling internationally for a family emergency, please fill out the short travel safety checklist in that hub so we can provide any country-specific guidance and emergency contacts.

Maya (Eng Manager): Appreciate this. Will share in 1:1s and remind my team about the urgent flag.

Eli (Benefits): If anyone wants a private sync about benefits interactions (visa, dependents coverage, etc.) DM me and I'll set up time.

Avery (People Ops): Final note: this policy is effective today. We'll host the quick webinar Monday and keep FAQ updated. If you have feedback on wording or edge cases, please @Avery or email people-ops@redwood.com. Thanks everyone. :pray:
